meta.title: Run progress
meta.description: Adds a slim progress rail pinned to the far right edge of the Web GUI while the agent is working, a live token readout beside it, and a run-flow panel behind both. The rail follows the Session shown in the main conversation: its colour and fill come from the current turn and, when the agent keeps a task list, from that list's completion instead of a made-up estimate; without a task list it shows a moving activity pulse. The vertical number under the bars is a percentage: the task progress when a task list exists (for example 33%), otherwise the context occupancy (yellow past 75%, red past 90%); no elapsed time is printed at the edge. A second thin bar shows how full the context window is, and the little pill below keeps the token sizes readable in real time (for example 12.3k/51.2k) with the Session's estimated cost in RMB (for example ≈¥0.63) even while the Session is idle; drag the pill anywhere on the window (the position is kept in this browser, not the Session log, and stays on screen when the window shrinks), and double-click it to return to the default seat — a drag never opens the panel by accident. Click the rail or the pill to open the Run flow panel: a Token section with context occupancy, input / cache read / cache write / output, the Session total, and the estimated cost broken down per bucket with the rates it used, then compact cards for the newest turns (up to eight): turn number, state, step count, elapsed time, one-line prompt and reply previews, and **a Token line on every turn** (that turn's reported input / cache read / cache write / output and its own estimated cost). **clicking a turn header** opens that turn's full detail — every step, every tool call with its whole argument summary, and the untruncated prompt and reply — and clicking again collapses it; nothing expands on hover, one card at a time. Plus the task list with a completion bar. Press Escape or click ✕ to close; the rail hides itself when the Session is idle and the last turn has settled. Read-only: it renders session events and token projections the browser already holds and never writes to the Session log. It shows one Session at a time — the one open in the main conversation — and keeps no history of its own. Token figures are provider-reported prompt-side samples plus the meter's estimate of surface movement, so treat them as a status readout, not billing. The RMB figure is a local estimate of the four token buckets times a price table this plugin carries (defaults ¥2 / ¥0.2 / ¥2 / ¥3 per 1M tokens, overridable through localStorage['dsh-run-progress:pricing']); it does not know about discounts, free tiers, or a route with different prices.
